Hyc Youth Courage Regd vs The State Of Telangana on 11
December, 2024
Author: B. Vijaysen Reddy
Bench: B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Honourable Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Writ Petition Nos.20333 And 17616 Of 2024
Common Order :

entities.text: Hyc Youth Courage Regd vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ORAL) Since the issue involved in these writ petitions is one and the same, both these writ petitions are disposed of by this common order.

Heard Mr. M. A. Mujeeb, learned counsel for the petitioner; Mr. Aashir Mehtab Khan, learned counsel for unofficial respondent (respondent No.4 in W.P. No.20333 of 2024 and respondent No.3 in W.P. No.17616 of 2024), and Mr. B. Sridhar, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home,
and perused the material on record.

This writ petition is filed by the petitioner seeking to declare the action of respondents No.2 and 3 in freezing its bank account vide A/c No.50200053877852,
as being illegal, arbitrary and unconstitutional.
4.

Order dated 26.09.2024 was passed by this Court in W.P. No.20333 of 2024 giving liberty to the petitioner to file application under Section 451 read with Section 457 Cr.P.C. for defreezing its bank account.

Accordingly, application was filed by the petitioner vide Crl. M. P. No.4513 of 2024 in Crime No.195 of 2024 on the file of the learned XII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hyderabad (for short 'learned Magistrate') which was dismissed by order dated 04.11.2024 on the ground that the investigation is pending.
5.

entities.text: XII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the action of the respondent authorities in freezing the bank account of the petitioner is illegal and requested this Court to pass orders to defreeze the bank account.

Learned counsel submitted that there is no compliance of the procedure contemplated under Section 102 Cr.P.C.
and there is inordinate delay in conducting investigation in Crime No.195 of 2024 registered with Saidabad Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 420 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Section 66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
Thus, the investigation conducted in the said crime to the extent of defreezing the bank account of the petitioner is vitiated and the cause of action still survives for adjudication.

7. In view of the dismissal order dated 04.11.2024 passed by the learned Magistrate in Crl.M.P.
No.4513 of 2024 in Crime No.195 of 2024, this Court is not inclined to continue this writ petition.

Accordingly, W.P. No.20333 of 2024 is disposed of giving liberty to the petitioner to file application either under Section 482 Cr.P.C. or Section 397 Cr.P.C. before the appropriate Courts challenging the order dated 04.11.2024.

W.P. No.17616 of 2024:
This writ petition is filed by the petitioner seeking to declare the action of respondent No.2 therein - the Additional Inspector of Police, Saidabad Police Station in freezing his bank account vide A/c No.39985894849 in connection with Crime No.150 of 2024 dated 15.04.2024 registered with Saidabad Police Station for the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), as being illegal,
arbitrary and unconstitutional.
9. In view of the order passed above in W.P. No.20333 of 2024, this writ petition is disposed of in terms thereof.
10. In the result, W.P. Nos.20333 of 2024 and 17616 of 2024 are disposed of and.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in these writ petitions, stand closed.
